messages.subject: physignal fonction for a specific clade
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a question related to the physignal function. I want to make sure that I'm doing it properly.

I have used the following command for my entire tree:

physignal(Y$coords,mytree,iter = 9999)


Now I would like to check the phylogenetic signal for specific clades, I have made a subset tree and and subset of my procrustes coordinates for a specific group:

YcoordSb<- Y$coords[,,1:22]

mytreeSb<-read.tree(file ="mytree2.tre")

physignal(YcoordSb,mytreeSb,iter = 9999)


However, I would like to know if there is a way to select a particular clade instead of creating a separate tree file. So I have created a variable that only include a specific clade using my original tree:

Clade1<-tips(mytree, mrca(mytree)["taxonA","taxonB"])


This returns all the taxa belonging to Clade 1; however I'm having a hard time integrating it into the phylosignal function, I tried something like that but it does not work:

physignal(YcoordSb,mytree$Clade1,iter = 9999)


Thank you so much for all the help you are providing to people like me! Thank you for taking the time to answer all our questions.


Ornella

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] physignal fonction for a specific clade
parts:
Ornella,

 

You need to match up the subset of species in the data with a pruned phylogeny. The following procedure is one way:

 

1: create reduced dataset: example: mydat.small<-mydata[,,1:22]

 

2: use the ‘treedata’ function In geiger to match reduced data  to tree:

  Matchdata<-treedata(phy = origphylogeny, data = mydat.small)

 

plot(Matchdata$phy)  #check to see that the pruned tree is what you want

 

3: physignal(mydat.small, Matchdata$phy)

 

Dean

parts:
Ornella,

 

If you have names for each object, these are found in the ‘third’ dimension of ‘dimnames’.  For instance, try:

 

library(geomorph)

data(plethspecies)

plethspecies$land

 

dimnames(plethspecies$land)  #shown another way.

 

If you then reduce part of the data, the names will come along with it, for instance:

 

plethspecies$land[,,1:3]

 

Check to see if your original data contained these names; that may be the problem.

Dean

On Friday, March 30, 2018 at 10:31:16 AM UTC-4, Dean Adams wrote:

Ornella,

 

If you have names for each object, these are found in the ‘third’ dimension of ‘dimnames’.  For instance, try:

 

library(geomorph)

data(plethspecies)

plethspecies$land

 

dimnames(plethspecies$land)  #shown another way.

 

If you then reduce part of the data, the names will come along with it, for instance:

 

plethspecies$land[,,1:3]

 

Check to see if your original data contained these names; that may be the problem.

On Thursday, March 29, 2018 at 12:52:15 PM UTC-4, Dean Adams wrote:

Ornella,

 

You need to match up the subset of species in the data with a pruned phylogeny. The following procedure is one way:

 

1: create reduced dataset: example: mydat.small<-mydata[,,1:22]

 

2: use the ‘treedata’ function In geiger to match reduced data  to tree:

  Matchdata<-treedata(phy = origphylogeny, data = mydat.small)

 

plot(Matchdata$phy)  #check to see that the pruned tree is what you want

 

3: physignal(mydat.small, Matchdata$phy)
